draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Kumily, the gateway to Thekkady! The lake inside Periyar Tiger Reserve isn't natural. It was made in 1895 by a dam, and dead tree stumps still stand in the water.
draft.hungryLine: Kumily smells of cardamom and pepper. Try a spice-garden lunch while you're here.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Take the morning boat on Periyar Lake, when elephants come down to drink.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk a spice plantation slowly and taste everything the guide hands you.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kumily sits right on the Tamil Nadu border. Walk a few minutes and the signs change language.

legends.title: Trees that refuse to fall
legends.body: When the dam flooded the valley, the forest went under. The tree stumps you see from the boat have stood in the water for over a century.

legends.title: The engineer who sold his things
legends.body: Colonel John Pennycuick built the dam. Locals say that when money ran short he sold his own property in England to finish it. In Tamil Nadu, villages still honour him.

tips.title: Take the first boat.
tips.body: Animals are out early, and the light is soft.

tips.title: Check cardamom grades.
tips.body: The bigger, greener pods cost more and are worth it.

story.title: Spice hills
story.body: These hills have grown pepper and cardamom for thousands of years. Traders from far away came looking for exactly what still grows in these gardens.

story.title: A dam across the Periyar
story.body: The British built the Mullaperiyar dam to send water east to the dry plains of Madurai. It flooded a valley and created the lake.

story.title: A protected forest
story.body: The forest around the lake became a game sanctuary. In 1978 it became a tiger reserve.

story.title: Forest guards from the forest
story.body: Some of the reserve's guides and protectors come from local tribal communities who once lived inside the forest. Their knowledge shapes how visitors walk it today.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Boat in the morning, spice garden after lunch and a Kathakali show at night. Tell me which spice you liked best.
